[0] everyday_reading (E): "Power" suggests strength or Math.pow on a number; here it means raising the transition matrix to the t-th power by multiplying a probability vector by p[][] t times.
[1] misconception (M) -> StartPageMatters: wrong rule: The page ranks depend on which page the surfer starts from. Right rule: The iteration converges to the same vector no matter where it starts; Markov starts from [1.0 0 0 0 0] only for convenience.
[2] misconception (M) -> OneIterationSuffices: wrong rule: One vector-matrix multiplication gives the exact page ranks. Right rule: One multiplication gives the probabilities after one move ([.02 .92 .02 .02 .02] from page 0); about 20 multiplications give two decimal places and 20 more give three.
[3] misconception (M) -> MatrixProductCommutes: wrong rule: A * B and B * A are the same matrix. Right rule: Matrix multiplication is not commutative: c[i][j] is row i of the left factor dotted with column j of the right; rank * p (row vector times matrix) is the page-rank update, p * rank is a different vector.
[4] inconsistent_trace (T) -> StartPageMatters: Applies LT (compute all of newRank from the old rank, then copy) unevenly: e.g. on some passes writing rank[j] directly so later j use partly updated values, or forgetting to recreate newRank so sums accumulate. (here mixing in: "The page ranks depend on which page the surfer starts from")

[0] names_the_element (N): An iterative algorithm: repeated vector-matrix multiplication of a probability vector by the transition matrix.
[1] states_the_rule (S): The vector of probabilities after t steps is the vector after t-1 steps times the transition matrix; by the basic limit theorem this converges to the same vector from any start.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): rank = [1, 0, ..., 0]; for each t: create newRank (zeros); for each j, for each k, newRank[j] += rank[k]*p[k][j]; then copy newRank into rank. Finally print rank.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Prints the page-rank vector after T multiplications: Markov 20 gives 0.27245 0.26515 0.14669 0.24764 0.06806 and Markov 40 gives 0.27303 0.26573 0.14618 0.24723 0.06783.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One iteration replaces every rank[j] with the dot product of the old rank and column j of p; the vector still sums to 1.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each iteration is a vector-matrix product: newRank[j] is the dot product of rank[] and column j of p[][], computed with nested for loops.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each multiplication is one move of the chain; convergence is the chain's mixing.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): Gives the move probabilities exactly (up to floating-point precision), whereas the simulation only estimates them.
[3] relation_to_neighbour (R): The number of iterations T controls accuracy: about 20 for two decimals and 20 more for three on tiny.txt.
[4] relation_to_neighbour (R): Computes the same ranks far more efficiently than simulating moves.
[5] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Iterative-refinement plan: repeat the same update until the vector stops changing; newRank[j] is a gatherer (dot product), rank is the state vector replaced each pass.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> StartPageMatters: Changing the start vector keeps the limit; more iterations keep the result and add digits; updating rank in place, or using p[j][k] instead of p[k][j], breaks the computation.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use when the transition matrix fits in memory and accurate ranks are needed: far more efficient than simulation; still too slow for the whole web, and repeated squaring is an alternative.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The new vector must be computed from the old vector only. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: rank[j] updated in place (no newRank): later columns use already-updated ranks, so the result is not rank * p (though it may still converge).
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: newRank must start at zero each iteration. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: newRank created once outside the t loop: sums accumulate across iterations and the vector grows beyond 1.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The update is rank (row) times p: use column j of p, p[k][j]. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Using p[j][k] (row j) computes p * rank instead, which does not give the page ranks.
[5] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Many iterations are needed for convergence. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: T too small (e.g. 1 or 2): prints the 1- or 2-move probabilities, not the ranks.

The power method used in Markov is far more efficient than simulating the behavior of a random surfer.
Each multiplication advances the chain's probabilities by one move.
The power method is repeated vector-matrix multiplication.
The convergence rate counts how many power-method multiplications are needed for a given accuracy: about 20 for two decimal places and 20 more for three.

The power method computes the move probabilities exactly (up to floating-point precision), in contrast to the simulation, which produces an estimate and needs more iterations to get a more accurate estimate.
The power method multiplies the rank vector by the transition matrix, stored as a two-dimensional array p[i][j].
